STRESS AND SLEEP
High stress levels and lack of adequate sleep are both associated 
with inflammation. Elevated circulating cortisol levels found 
under conditions of psychological stress are associated with ele-
vated inflammatory cytokines. Sustained sleep restriction has 
also been associated with an inflammatory state and an elevation 
of TNF- a, IL -1b, IL-2, IL-4 and monocyte chemo-attractant 
protein-1 (MCP-1). (Axelsson et al, 2013) Intentionally practic-
ing stress reduction techniques such as meditation has been 
shown to reduce the inflammatory response in human experi-
mental models (Kox et al, 2014).
